gloss: to become diluted; to weaken; to fade

definitions.gloss: to become diluted, to become thinner, to weaken
definitions.explanation: For a liquid, color, flavor, or abstract quality to become weaker or less concentrated. Used for both physical dilution (soup becoming watery) and figurative weakening (interest fading, impressions dimming).

examples.japanese: スープの{味|あじ}が{薄|うす}まった。
{時間|じかん}がたつにつれて{記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}まっていく。
examples.english: As time passes, memories gradually fade.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}を{足|た}しすぎて{紅茶|こうちゃ}の{色|いろ}がすっかり{薄|うす}まってしまった。
examples.english: I added too much water, and the color of the tea became completely washed out.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Godan verb ({五段|ごだん}). {薄|うす}まる → {薄|うす}まらない → {薄|うす}まって → {薄|うす}まった

USAGE:
The intransitive counterpart of {薄|うす}める (to dilute, to weaken). {薄|うす}まる describes the change happening on its own, while {薄|うす}める implies someone deliberately diluting something. Can be used for physical properties (flavor, color, concentration) and abstract qualities (memories, impressions, suspicion).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {味|あじ}が{薄|うす}まる: flavor becomes diluted
- {記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}まる: memories fade
- {色|いろ}が{薄|うす}まる: color fades
- {印象|いんしょう}が{薄|うす}まる: impression weakens
